code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
description: Armed clashes between forces move into or near the settlement.
respondent_phrasing: The fighting reached our village and we ran.
sources: IDMC IAC/NIAC; ACLED Armed clash; UCDP state-based

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
description: Air strikes, drone strikes, artillery or missile attack on populated areas.
respondent_phrasing: Shells landed on the houses near us.

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
description: Land or routes made unusable by mines and unexploded ordnance, often blocking return as much as causing flight.
respondent_phrasing: The road and the fields were mined so we could not stay.

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
description: A different armed actor takes over the area; people flee the incoming authority rather than the fighting itself.
respondent_phrasing: The other side took the town, so we left.
sources: ACLED Government regains territory; ACLED Non-state actor overtakes territory

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
mechanism: Siege, encirclement, starvation as a method of war
description: Movement and supplies cut off until leaving is the only option.
respondent_phrasing: Nothing could get in or out for months.

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
mechanism: Forced recruitment or conscription by armed actors
description: Families leave to prevent sons or daughters being taken.
respondent_phrasing: They came to take the young men, so we sent them away and then followed.
sources: DTM Forced recruitment; HRW on M23

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
mechanism: Anticipatory flight ahead of an advancing front
description: Leaving BEFORE violence arrives, on the basis of what happened elsewhere. Invisible to event data by definition - there is no event at the origin.
respondent_phrasing: We left before they arrived because we heard what they did in the next district.

code_label: Threat of armed conflict or war
mechanism: Home or infrastructure destroyed, making return impossible
description: The displacement continues because there is nothing to return to.
respondent_phrasing: Our house was destroyed, so even when it was calm we could not go back.

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
mechanism: Communal violence over land, water or grazing
description: Violence between communities over resources, frequently seasonal and recurrent.
respondent_phrasing: Two communities started fighting over the wells and the grazing land.
sources: IDMC OSV; ACLED Mob violence; UCDP non-state

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
description: Gangs or cartels exercising de facto control, extorting and expelling.
respondent_phrasing: The gang took over our neighbourhood and told families to go.

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
description: Crowd violence targeting people, homes or businesses.
respondent_phrasing: A crowd came through and burned the shops.
sources: ACLED Mob violence; ACLED Violent demonstration

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
description: State or para-state force used against protesters. Straddles this option and code 4.
respondent_phrasing: They fired on the demonstration and afterwards came looking for people.

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
description: Armed raids on livestock and stores that strip livelihoods and force movement.
respondent_phrasing: They came for the cattle and burned what was left.

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
description: Abduction as an economic activity, producing pre-emptive flight.
respondent_phrasing: They were taking people from the road for money, so we moved to the town.

code_label: Widespread violence or breakdown of public order
mechanism: Collapse of policing - no protection available
description: Not an event but an absence. Nothing in event data records the non-arrival of police.
respondent_phrasing: There was nobody to stop it and nobody to complain to.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
mechanism: Screening by ethnicity, tribe or language at checkpoints
description: Identity checked at a barrier and treatment decided by the answer.
respondent_phrasing: At the checkpoint they asked what tribe we were.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: A group given hours or days to leave on the basis of who they are.
respondent_phrasing: They gave all of us of our religion one day to be out of the town.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Conversion demanded, worship prevented, places of worship destroyed.
respondent_phrasing: They said we had to convert or go, and they burned the church.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Targeted for party affiliation, voting, activism or association.
respondent_phrasing: My son worked at the polling table for the opposition, and then they marked our door.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Persecuted for the language spoken or the region of origin, not ethnicity as usually defined.
respondent_phrasing: They called us names because we speak English and said we were all with the fighters.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Groups without armed protection dispossessed by stronger ones; ascribed inferior status.
respondent_phrasing: We are from a small group with no gunmen of our own, so a stronger group took our farm.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Citizenship legally withheld, making a whole population expellable.
respondent_phrasing: They said we do not belong to this country and we have no citizenship card.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
mechanism: Persecution on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity
description: Criminalisation, mob violence, family expulsion, blackmail.
respondent_phrasing: People found out about me and I could not stay in my own family's area.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Papers taken so that return, movement or proof of ownership becomes impossible.
respondent_phrasing: They took our identity papers before they let us cross.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
description: Attacked for an identity the attacker assigned, not one held. A question about the respondent's own group membership can miss this entirely.
respondent_phrasing: They killed anyone carrying a government card - it was the paper, not who we were.

code_label: Discrimination or persecution
mechanism: Discriminatory denial of aid, services or land rights
description: Not violence, but exclusion severe enough that staying is untenable.
respondent_phrasing: We were not allowed to register for the food, and could not get work.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Held without charge or trial; families flee before the next round.
respondent_phrasing: They took my brother and he has never been to court.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Released detainees and their families leave.
respondent_phrasing: They beat him for months and when they let him out they kept watching him.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Taken by officials or men in uniform and never accounted for.
respondent_phrasing: Men in uniform came at night and we never saw him again.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: The one part of code 4 that global data does count.
respondent_phrasing: The soldiers shot people in the street during the operation.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
mechanism: Confiscation or destruction of property by authorities
description: Named explicitly in the option, and almost entirely uncounted.
respondent_phrasing: They put a seal on the house and said it was taken.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Housing destroyed as collective punishment rather than for a project.
respondent_phrasing: They destroyed our part of the neighbourhood because of who lived there.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
mechanism: Eviction from a displacement site by authorities
description: Being displaced a second time, by the state, from a camp or settlement.
respondent_phrasing: The commissioner came with a bulldozer and destroyed the shelter.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
mechanism: Banishment or denial of return through security screening
description: Not why people LEFT but why they cannot go back. The stem 'have you ever left a home due to' misses this.
respondent_phrasing: Because my brother's name was on a list they will not let us back into the neighbourhood.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Fleeing the draft or indefinite national service.
respondent_phrasing: He would have been taken for national service with no end, so he left.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
mechanism: Surveillance and explicit threat by officials
description: No arrest, but a credible warning that compels flight.
respondent_phrasing: They told him to stop working and that they were watching him.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Papers, permits or registration withheld until life becomes unworkable.
respondent_phrasing: They would not give us the papers, so we could not work or travel.

code_label: Threat of human rights violations by authorities
description: Expelled back across a border. Afghanistan's largest current flow, and NO response option covers it.
respondent_phrasing: We were put on a bus at the border and sent back.

code_label: Other threats of violence against you
description: A message, a mark on the door, a list. Arrives as a personal threat even when the driver is political.
respondent_phrasing: They put a mark on our door and we understood we had to go.

code_label: Other threats of violence against you
description: Massively under-reported in every source, and straddles codes 3, 4 and 5 depending on perpetrator and motive.
respondent_phrasing: What happened to my daughter meant we could not stay there.

code_label: Other threats of violence against you
description: Taken by armed or criminal groups rather than authorities.
respondent_phrasing: They took him and we never found out who they were.

code_label: Other threats of violence against you
description: Inter-family cycles of retaliation that displace whole households.
respondent_phrasing: After the killing, the other family would come for us.

code_label: Other threats of violence against you
mechanism: Accusation of witchcraft or ritual violence
description: Documented as a displacement driver in Haiti; likely present elsewhere and invisible.
respondent_phrasing: They said the old people were doing witchcraft and started killing them.

code_label: Other threats of violence against you
description: Whether this belongs in a forced-displacement instrument at all is a live question - but people will report it, so enumerators need a rule.
respondent_phrasing: I left because of my husband.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: The single largest disaster mechanism worldwide by people displaced.
respondent_phrasing: The water came into the houses and did not go down.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: Largest single hazard sub-type in IDMC's data.
respondent_phrasing: The storm took the roof off and the whole area was flattened.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: Slow-onset. A household that left over three seasons may not describe it as fleeing at all.
respondent_phrasing: The rains failed three times, the animals died, and there was nothing left.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: Sudden, and usually followed by a return question rather than a leaving question.
respondent_phrasing: The house came down in the earthquake.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: Often triggered by rain, sometimes by deforestation or quarrying - a code 6/7 boundary case.
respondent_phrasing: The hillside came down onto the houses below.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: Includes long evacuation periods with no defined return.
respondent_phrasing: The mountain started throwing ash and they moved everybody out.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: The slowest onset of all; displacement is gradual and rarely recorded as an event.
respondent_phrasing: The sea has taken the land where our house was, a little each year.

code_label: Natural disasters
description: Cold waves and heat events; small in the data, real for the households affected.
respondent_phrasing: The cold killed the animals and we could not stay through it.

code_label: Natural disasters
mechanism: Pre-emptive evacuation ahead of a hazard
description: Left before impact on an official warning. Large in IDMC's flow figures and the most likely mismatch with 'had to flee a home'.
respondent_phrasing: They told us a storm was coming and moved us for a week.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Land permanently flooded by a planned reservoir. Merowe 50,000+, Makhoul 100,000+.
respondent_phrasing: They are building a dam and our village will be under the water.
sources: qualitative: FMR Sudan, Save the Tigris Iraq

code_label: Man-made events
description: Communities cleared for extraction, sometimes with houses marked for demolition.
respondent_phrasing: The mining company said the land was theirs and put marks on the houses.
sources: qualitative: Amnesty DRC, ROAPE Burkina Faso

code_label: Man-made events
description: 'Beautification', modernisation and clearance of informal settlements.
respondent_phrasing: They marked our neighbourhood for the new city project and knocked it down.

code_label: Man-made events
mechanism: Transport infrastructure - roads, ports, airports, rail
description: Route and terminal construction displacing settlements along the line.
respondent_phrasing: They said the village had to go because of the new port.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Land allocated to commercial agriculture over existing users.
respondent_phrasing: They took our grazing land along the river for the sugar farm.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Water, soil or air made unusable. Harm is well documented; displacement attribution is thin.
respondent_phrasing: The waste got into the water, the fish and cattle died, and people moved away.
sources: qualitative: Amnesty Niger Delta, RVI South Sudan

code_label: Man-made events
description: Flaring, produced-water discharge and land take around fields.
respondent_phrasing: The gas flare burns beside the houses all night.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Rare, enormous, permanent. Chornobyl relocated ~350,000 - within a respondent's lifetime.
respondent_phrasing: After the reactor exploded they told us the whole town had to leave and never come back.

code_label: Man-made events
description: A structure operating or failing rather than a natural hazard. Counted by IDMC, but filed under Disaster.
respondent_phrasing: They opened the dam and the water came down onto us.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Land cleared for private development. Somalia: 1.5m people affected 2018-2024.
respondent_phrasing: They came early with tractors and pulled down our shelter to build apartments.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Communities removed to create or enforce parks and reserves. Documented globally, counted nowhere.
respondent_phrasing: They made it a park and told us we could no longer live or graze inside.

code_label: Man-made events
description: Ground collapse caused by mining or groundwater withdrawal.
respondent_phrasing: The ground opened up where they had been pumping.

code_label: A different threat to you or your family's safety
description: By design this has no sub-taxonomy. Its content IS the enrichment mechanism: verbatim responses here are the only route by which mechanisms nobody has anticipated enter the classification.
